known_limits: ARM64 is explicitly unsupported by this canonical Intel plugin.
Default listing enumerates all active processes; real differential evidence currently covers PID 4 only. Synthetic tests cover all/selected/absent PID behavior.
Attached pagefiles and highest-address behavior have synthetic coverage; real listing cases cover Server2003 non-PAE, Server2008 PAE and three x64 samples. Explicit attachment provenance is retained.
The pinned maximum-address invocation excludes the final virtual byte. x64 rows retain raw lower 48-bit virtual addresses.
Windows x64 uses the pinned 45-bit PFN mask for transition mappings. This projection does not change the general virtual-memory translator.
Zero keeps diagnostics for unavailable physical spans, unreadable/uniform tables, absent explicit paging attachments and resource limits. These cases remain partial.
Per-process traversal stops at 262144 tables or 1000000 merged intervals; combined output also stops at 1000000 intervals with partial diagnostics. Cancellation propagates.

Exports require one explicit nonzero PID, reject address-range arguments, and enforce a 256 MiB limit. Reference all-process and larger exports are deliberately not enabled under the repository targeted-export policy.
Exports bypass result-cache reads and writes and use atomic files with SHA256/byte-count metadata. Raw recovered bytes remain ignored under target/.
The original reported Debian LiME image is unavailable; this Windows work does not establish a fix for its init_task/page-table validation failure.
development_findings: The first real run was rejected by public PID validation because the Memmap contract has no PID output column; explicit Memmap PID validation was added before final differential runs.

The initial regression baseline accidentally ran PID 4 row counts without their filter. Baselines now declare row_options and acceptance passes those exact options; final Windows regression passed all 13 available cases.
A synthetic test initially attempted to clone Isf; it now reparses its fixture data. Final build, Clippy and tests passed.
